newsitem.title: FRANCE: REUTERS FRENCH ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST -JUNE 30.
newsitem.headline: REUTERS FRENCH ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST -JUNE 30.

text.p: REUTERS FRENCH ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet and Brand-name Products.
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

CANNES - A series of two ads for Diesel jeans created by the Swedish advertising agency Paradist DDB Stockholm won the top prize at the annual International Advertising Festival here, a member of the jury says. (Reuter)
PARIS - Pierre Dauzier, chairman of French media group Havas, says the Havas board will not look at proposals to divest from weekly news magazines Le Point and L'Express until September.
(Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

PARIS - Canal Plus is preparing to leave the German television market and focus on other European countries it finds more promising, particularly Italy, the pay television group's top executives say. The company will decide in August whether it goes ahead with plans to launch a news channel.(Reuter)
PARIS - Christian Perret, France's Industry Minister, wants the European Union to regulate the type of information available on the Internet. (Les Echos)
PARIS - French pay television company Canal Plus says it maintains its March forecast that the cost of absorbing Dutch-based Nethold would leave it close to breakeven in 1997.
(Reuter)

PARIS - The French telecommunications regulator ART will give its verdict by the end of July on a row between France's cablte television operators and France Telecom over the price of them offering Internet access via cable networks. (Les Echos)

PARIS - Jean-Marie Messier, chairman of France's Compagnie Generale des Eaux (CGE), says he does not rule out any options in the sale of cable unit Compagnie Generale de Videcommunication (CGV). (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

PARIS - Family-controlled drinks group Pernod Ricard aims to keep its independence despite the impending creation of a drinks giant if the planned Guinness-Grand Met merger goes ahead. Chairman Patrick Ricard says an alliance is not the group's top priority. (Le Figaro)

LONDON - The heads of Guinness PLC and Grand Metropolitan PLC will go to Paris to meet LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault on Wednesday in an effort to open the way to a merger of the three companies, a source close to Guinness says. LVMH declines comment on a British newspaper report that the two British firms had made secret overtures to it over such a merger. (Reuter)
PARIS - French carmaker Renault says it will go ahead and close a Belgian factory employing around 3,000 workers, despite heavy government and trade union pressure to consider alternatives.
(Reuter)
Paris Editorial, Sue Landau
